_note: Heat-exchanger geometry for plantagent/hxdetail.py. Every field names its source; ILLUSTRATIVE marks values that are not in the patent, the P&ID or the data sheet (typical construction for the service, to be replaced by the vendor data sheet).

E-201.service: VRC evaporator forced-circulation heater: saturated NaCl brine slurry in the tubes, compressor-discharge steam condensing on the shell

model_U.why: the model folds E-201 into the V-201 evaporator heating (area 8,800 m2, U 2,000 W/m2K in service, 2,500 W/m2K clean on the data sheet)

cold.source: data sheet: brine in V-201 saturated in salt; solubility from plantagent/brine.py x_sat at the heater inlet temperature

hot.source: data sheet: steam to E-201 after D-201 at 3.08 bar(a), condensate leaves saturated

rise_K.source: data sheet Process requirements: brine temperature rise through E-201 at most 3 K

rated_m3_h.source: data sheet Equipment ratings: P-201 forced-circulation pump 15,000 m3/h rated (ILLUSTRATIVE)

area_m2.source: data sheet Equipment ratings (E-201 8,800 m2, ILLUSTRATIVE in the data sheet)

tube_od_m.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: 1.5 in tubes, common in salt-slurry heaters to limit plugging

baffle_spacing_m.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: tube-support spacing near the TEMA maximum unsupported span for 1.5 in tubes (no cross-flow baffles on a condensing shell)

tube_k_W_mK.source: ILLUSTRATIVE material titanium grade 2 (handbook thermal conductivity about 16 W/m K)

tube.source: typical practice for saturated NaCl brine circulation: 0.001 h ft2 F/Btu (no TEMA RGP-T-2.4 entry for crystallising brine; scaling is governed by velocity and supersaturation)

shell.source: TEMA RGP-T-2.4: steam, oil-free, 0.0005 h ft2 F/Btu

tube_velocity_min_m_s.source: typical practice for forced-circulation crystalliser heaters (1.5-3 m/s): below it the slurry settles and the tubes scale

dP_tube_max_bar.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: part of the P-201 differential 1.33 bar (model) available to the heater

dP_shell_max_bar.source: typical practice for a condensing-steam shell at 3 bar(a): a few % of the absolute pressure
